t: This is 59 Old Compton Street in Soho, once the 2i's Coffee Bar, which was open from 1956 to 1970. It played a formative part in the rise of Britain's skiffle and rock and roll scene in the late fifties. Several major stars, including Tommy Steele and Cliff Richard, were first discovered performing here. The coffee bar was owned by Paul Lincoln, an Australian professional wrestler and promoter, who also went by the ring name Dr. Death.
